title: A spring Pacific temperature contrast gave no clear added winter forecast gain in a linear test for 1981-2024
abstract: We tested whether the March-May Nino 1+2 minus Nino 4 temperature anomaly adds skill for the following December-February Nino 3.4 anomaly. The baseline used spring strength, its change from winter, and an absolute centered-strength term. We used a fixed NOAA CPC ERSSTv5 table, 30 initial training years and 44 forecasts from 1981 to 2024. Each fit used earlier origin years only. The contrast reduced mean squared error by 0.0101 C squared, or 1.31%. The conditional 95% five-year block interval was -0.0804 to 0.1015 C squared. Root mean squared error changed from 0.8774 to 0.8716 C. The gain was positive in the first half and negative in the second half. All planned model checks had intervals that included zero. Thus, this test gives no clear added forecast gain. It does not show equal skill or identify a physical cause. One revised SST product, few independent events, model form and conditional uncertainty limit the result. The package includes the source snapshot, each forecast, code, uncertainty draws and an independent numerical audit.

display.caption: Observed and predicted winter anomalies, annual paired error gains, and model checks. Positive gain means lower error with the contrast. All model-check 95% five-year block intervals include zero.
